Local tailoring and stakeholder engagement

3.200 You are required to build strong and effective relationships with PTWAs, employers and wider stakeholders. This is essential to the successful delivery of Confident Futures. You must utilise and build on the partnership and engagement approaches established through Confident Futures ensuring Participants are effectively connected to local employment opportunities and appropriate community-based support.

3.201 You must ensure Confident Futures is well integrated with local and specialist services within each CPA. This includes working collaboratively with relevant agencies to make effective use of local funding streams, expertise and provision, enabling Participants particularly those with complex barriers to work to receive coordinated and holistic support. Providers must actively work to avoid duplication of provision and ensure support is aligned across services.

3.202 To support the above requirements, you will be required to:

maintain strong, ongoing engagement with all stakeholders within each Contract Package Area (CPA) to inform the design, implementation and delivery of the Services the Supplier provides

strengthen collaborative working by hosting or contributing to partnership forums and meetings that promote alignment, effective communication and coordinated delivery with all stakeholders

adopt a joined-up approach to employer engagement, working collaboratively with other providers to manage national and large employer accounts whose vacancies span multiple CPAs

develop and maintain relationships with local employers and stakeholders to source suitable vacancies, work opportunities and progression routes as Participants become job ready

upskill employers, where required, to support them in offering inclusive, sustainable employment opportunities aligned with the needs of Participants

utilise and enhance links with local services, health bodies and community organisations to ensure Participants can access appropriate support and Provision that meets their individual needs

place a strong focus on addressing and ensuring coordinated support for health-related barriers to employment by developing and maintaining effective working relationships with relevant local health partners

engage with relevant stakeholders at appropriate intervals to share good practice, exchange information effectively, resolve delivery issues and align support packages for Participants, including engagement with:

Jobcentre Plus Partnership Managers

Employment Account Division (EAD) Performance Managers (or equivalent) of the authority

local authorities

training suppliers

employer forums

sector specific bodies

other relevant stakeholders as required

engage with organisations represented on established local Get Britain Working Partnership Boards in England

engage with organisations represented through Regional Skills Partnerships, Public Services Boards, Regional Partnership Boards and Regional Engagement Teams in Wales

take the lead in establishing and facilitating regular partnership engagement meetings where partnership forums do not exist within a CPA

3.203 Due to the particular needs of the Participant group, a focus on support for health conditions will be a key element of this provision. As such, you must develop and maintain effective working relationships with relevant local health partners to ensure coordinated support for Participants’ health-related barriers.

3.204 You should engage with relevant stakeholders at appropriate intervals to share good practice, exchange information effectively, resolve delivery issues and align support packages for Participants, including engagement with:

Jobcentre Plus Partnership Managers

DWP EAD Performance Managers (or equivalent)

local authorities

training providers

employer forums

sector‑specific bodies

other relevant stakeholders as required

3.205 In England, engage with organisations represented on established local Get Britain Working Partnership Boards.

3.206 In Wales, engage with organisations represented through Regional Skills Partnerships, Public Services Boards, Regional Partnership Boards and Regional Engagement Teams.

3.207 A proactive and structured approach to stakeholder engagement should underpin delivery, supported by a clear local engagement plan that reflects labour market conditions, stakeholder priorities, and Participant needs. This should ensure early connection with key partners and sustained, meaningful engagement to support effective service integration.

3.208 Expectations around stakeholder and local engagement should be evidenced through the Participant Support Summary and Delivery Review outputs. These should clearly demonstrate how engagement activity:

supports effective local integration

reflects labour market demand

enables tailored Participant journeys and outcomes

Employer engagement

3.209 A dedicated and structured approach to employer engagement should form a core component of delivery, aligning with Disability Confident principles and the broader aims of Confident Futures. This should include proactive engagement with a diverse range of employers, including Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and those with limited experience of recruiting or supporting individuals with health conditions or disabilities.

3.210 Engagement activity should focus on building employer awareness, understanding, and commitment to inclusive recruitment practices. This includes promoting the benefits of disability inclusion and encouraging employers to identify and offer suitable opportunities for Participants.

3.61 If the Dedicated Adviser fails to contact the Participant within one working day of their failure to attend the meeting, they shall note their attempts at contact on the Participant’s Support Plan and begin the disengagement process. You shall attempt to contact the Participant daily, at different times of day, over 5 working days, taking into account what is reasonable and, proportionate to the Participant’s circumstances as set out in their Support Plan.

3.62 The Dedicated Adviser shall then attempt to make contact with the Participant once every 5 working days for the next 15 working days. You shall record on the Participant’s Support Plan the method(s) of communication used to contact the Participant, the date(s) and time(s) of attempted contact.

3.63 If contact is re-established, you should discuss the reasons for non-contact. If the Participant confirms that they no longer wish to continue on the programme, notify the PTWA, via the designated Jobcentre Plus in box, of this using notification form UCCF02, and take the required action on PRAP to end the Participants time on programme. Refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment (PRaP) System for Confident Futures and refer to end codes. If the Participant wishes to continue on the programme, notify the PTWA using the notification form, UCCF02 to arrange the Six-Month Touchpoint meeting, which they will arrange within 15 working days of receipt of the form.

3.64 Exceptionally, the Participant may confirm to you that they wish to continue their participation on the programme beyond day 182, but do not want to take part in a Six-Month Touchpoint meeting. You should encourage the Participant to take part in the Touchpoint and remind them that it is designed to support their ongoing needs. If they still do not wish to participate, note this and their reasons on the Support Plan, and notify the PTWA using the UCCF02 notification form that a Six-Month Touchpoint meeting will not be required, and the Participant will be continuing on provision.

3.65 If the Participant decides to end their time on the Provision and return to Jobcentre Plus support, the Six-Month Touchpoint should act as a Warm Handback to the PTWA.

3.66 The Support Plan must be updated and the outcome and agreed next steps captured and shared with the Participant within 10 working days of the Six-Month Touchpoint being complete, in line with CSS 3.

3.67 Where a Participant’s Universal Credit claim ends before they reach the point at which a Six-Month Touchpoint would normally be arranged, the Six-Month Touchpoint process set out in the Specification and this guidance will not apply, and there will be no requirement to send the UCCF02 notification form to Jobcentre Plus.

3.68 At the point that a Six-Month Touchpoint would normally be carried out, you may undertake a structured review of the Participant’s progress, ongoing support needs and future goals and record the outcome within the Support Plan, including confirming that the Participant wishes to continue receiving support on Confident Futures up to day 365. All other Confident Futures delivery, record-keeping, performance management and contractual reporting requirements remain unchanged.

Chapter 3a: Referring Participants to Additional Support Provision

3.69 Confident Futures is a specific stage within a wider, holistic support pathway: from identification and assessment, through targeted confidence and capability-building support, to onward progression for some into work-focussed activity and support offers such as Connect to Work, for other Participants, employment.

3.70 You shall help Participants to access other relevant services for which they are eligible so that the Confident Futures Services are experienced as part of a coherent package of support. When Participants are referred to other services, you shall ensure an effective exchange of information to help deliver a seamless service to the Participant. Any exchange must be in accordance with the Data Protection Act 2018 and the UK GDPR.

3.71 A Participant cannot receive support through both Confident Futures and another DWP-funded employment support programme concurrently. Where the provider becomes aware that a Participant has been referred to or started on Connect to Work, they should notify the PTWA (using UCCF02 notification form) so that the most appropriate support can be agreed.

3.72 Where a Participant has support needs which are above and beyond those that will be addressed by Confident Futures, additional provision may be considered. The decision to refer a Confident Futures Participant to additional provision should be made jointly with the Participant; it must be deemed to be in their best interest and not in any way affect their ability to participate fully in Confident Futures.

3.73 Where individual needs are identified, consideration may be given to sourcing appropriate additional support outside of Confident Futures to best meet the Participant’s requirements.

3.74 There is a wide range of provision available to Participants, both nationally and locally, to help them obtain the skills and experience they need to start work, gain more work or better paid work. This provision can be organised into 4 main types of support:

DWP-funded employment support programme: A Participant on Confident Futures cannot be referred to any additional DWP Contracted Employment Provision. It is the responsibility of Confident Futures provider to source and fund all appropriate mental health support for Participants who require it whilst on this programme, however Access to Work (AtW) and AtW Mental Health Support Service (MHSS) can be used to support someone in employment

3.105 During engagement with your Participant, you may identify their behaviour or communication as being unusual, for example they may appear frustrated or angry, or may provide brief or one-word answers. Other indicators may help you in identifying and supporting your Participants, in addition to discussions with them and information from Jobcentre Plus. For example non-physical signs such as extreme weight loss and paranoia may indicate addiction, attending appointments with family or friends may indicate learning difficulties.

3.106 You should also consider the involvement of your Participant’s appointee or representative, where they have one, as they may provide additional information to help you provide the most appropriate type of support. Refer to Chapter 3: Supporting Participants on Confident Futures Appointee section.

3.107 All Participants should be aware of support they can access whilst taking part in Confident Futures. This support may include local initiatives and organisations identifiable via your organisation’s local engagement activity and agreed sharing of information methodology. You must signpost your Participants appropriately should they require access to any suitable and available support.

Note: It is important that you maintain professional boundaries when supporting Participants and signposting them to appropriate support. DWP does not require you to make formal referrals to this support as part of Confident Futures.

Note: Where you choose to share your Participants’ information with other organisations you must only do so in line with UK GDPR requirements.

3.108 As a Confident Futures provider, you are permitted to undertake home visits to Participants. However, these should only happen in exceptional circumstances where a safeguarding concern exists. Ensure you consider and implement your own ‘keeping safe’ policy during any home visit.

3.109 You must have safeguarding measures in place to protect the health and well-being of Participants during their time on provision, and to make sure they are supported in getting access to the help they need. You are required to engage with your Participants using a variety of methods which are reflective of their individual circumstances. This must also take into account any known or potential vulnerabilities where you or a PTWA have safeguarding concerns.

3.110 DWP does not prescribe the safeguarding measures which you should include in your approach. However, to support the DWPs safeguarding approach, you should incorporate the following elements within your approach:

prevention - the Participant shall remain at the heart of the approach. You should identify problems which may cause safeguarding concerns, including actions undertaken by you (DA). The adviser should take actions to address this as quickly as possible before harm occurs

review and continuous improvement - you should frequently review and update your safeguarding policy in response to customer experience and emerging safeguarding concerns

awareness of available support - Participants who may be or become a safeguarding concern must be aware of the support available and able to access it during their time on Provision. You should ensure all staff members are familiar with the safeguarding policy and are aware of how they can access available support where appropriate. Participants shall be encouraged to make their own decisions and access support without intrusion

Working with a Participant’s appointee or representative

3.111 A Participant may have an appointee or a representative. It is important to establish whether the person is an appointee or a representative as this will establish how to include this person in your interaction with the Participant. If the Claimant has an appointee at the referral stage, they are eligible to start Confident Futures.

3.112 You will be notified by the PTWA during the referral process where your Participant has a representative. A referral can be made if they have an appointee at referral stage. Similarly, you will be notified by the PTWA via the UCCF01 change of circumstances form where your Participant authorises an appointee or nominates a representative during their time on Confident Futures.

3.113 Where your Participant has an appointee, you should include them in all your discussions as they are responsible for acting on your Participant’s behalf in all dealings with the DWP whilst on Confident Futures. This includes their engagement and participation with you. They will be key to gaining information about your Participant’s circumstances and agreeing appropriate activities during their time on Confident Futures. Appointees are legally empowered to act on behalf of your Participant and there is no need to secure permission to disclose information to them.

3.114 You may wish to engage with your Participant’s representative, where they have one, for example during the first few interactions during their time on Confident Futures or inviting them to attend your interviews. Representatives do not have the same status as appointees but can be valuable in helping your Participant and yourselves during engagement. You must ensure you have your Participant’s explicit consent before disclosing information with their representative.

Participants where English is not their first language or where there are additional communication needs
